better: Run A is the better fine-tuning run for the task, but the frozen-setting KID table alone does not show it, and the reason matters. Under the frozen ILVR setting (strength 0.8) Run B has the lowest KID (56.0 x1e-3 vs 85.0 for Run A and 84.5 for the unchanged input photos) and the lowest FID (218.2), yet its LPIPS to the input is only 0.069: its outputs are the input photos with small low-level changes (Figure 8), not portraits in the MetFaces style. Run A changes the image substantially (LPIPS 0.313), but under ILVR with strength 0.8 its outputs are smoothed rather than painted and its KID does not improve on the input photos. With plain SDEdit (strength 0.6, fixed in advance, no guidance) Run A gives by far the best scores of the whole study, KID 46.8 and FID 193.1, against 65.3 / 230.7 for Run B and 140.8 / 246.7 for Run 0, and its outputs are the only ones that look like Old Masters portraits (Figure 8, last column). The difference between the runs is visible from the first saved checkpoint (epoch 1): Run A already repaints skin, hair and background (LPIPS 0.315), whereas Run B returns the photo (LPIPS 0.117, falling to 0.069 by epoch 10 as it learns to remove its small noise more faithfully). After epoch 1 neither run changes much: Run A's KID rises from 79.0 at epoch 1 to 93.5 at epoch 6 and recovers to 86.4 at epoch 20; Run B's stays between 52.4 and 57.5 (Figure 5).
mechanism: Image-to-image translation with a DDPM works only if the forward process at the start timestep destroys the photo's fine detail, so that the fine-tuned prior can repaint it. Under beta_t the start timestep t = 780 has alpha_bar_t = 0.0021: x_t = 0.05 x_0 + 1.00 eps keeps only the coarse layout (restored by ILVR) and the MetFaces-trained network generates new texture; this is why Run A changes the image (LPIPS 0.31-0.39) and, with SDEdit, moves the output distribution closest to MetFaces. Under beta_t^2 the same timestep has alpha_bar_t = 0.94: x_t = 0.97 x_0 + 0.25 eps still contains essentially the whole photograph, so whatever the network learned, the reverse process can only remove a small amount of noise and must return the input (LPIPS 0.05-0.07); even at t = T, alpha_bar_T = 0.87, so no strength setting can reach a noise level from which a new style could be generated. The same mathematics explains training: Run B's network only ever sees high-SNR inputs (log-SNR >= 1.9) and learns to predict a tiny noise component, giving a larger MSE (0.163 vs 0.011) and no ability to generate painterly content from noise. Run B's lower KID is therefore not translation: the light denoising slightly smooths camera noise and JPEG texture, which moves Inception statistics a little toward the (smooth, low-noise) MetFaces scans while the image stays the same photograph.
run0: Run 0, the pretrained CelebA-HQ model, has the worst KID in every setting (145.6 with ILVR, 140.8 with SDEdit), much worse than the unchanged input photos (84.5). Its prior is the CelebA-HQ photograph domain, so it 'repaints' each input as a cleaner photograph (Figure 2) and pulls it away from MetFaces. Fine-tuning under the native schedule re-targets that prior to the out-of-distribution painting domain with only 1,069 images and 20 epochs: with the same sampler Run A lowers KID from 140.8 to 46.8 and FID from 246.7 to 193.1. Fine-tuning under beta_t^2 also moves the scores away from Run 0, but mainly because the modified forward process stops the sampler from changing the photo, not because the model learned the new domain. Fine-tuning on an out-of-distribution dataset is effective only when the noise schedule lets the model see, and therefore learn to denoise from, inputs where the source content has been destroyed.
takeaway: The exponent on the noise schedule is not a mild hyperparameter. Squaring beta_t (x = 2.00) shrinks the total injected noise from 10.05 to 0.13 and leaves alpha_bar_T = 0.87, so the forward process never reaches the Gaussian prior and a DDPM fine-tuned with it can only lightly denoise, not translate. Native-schedule fine-tuning (Run A) was the only condition that produced recognisable Old Masters toonification, and it did so from the first epoch. We also learned three practical lessons: KID alone can reward an output that barely changes the input, so a metric of change (LPIPS to the input) and visual inspection must accompany it; every source of sampling noise has to be seeded, since unseeded per-step noise moved KID by about 8 x1e-3 between identical runs; and the inference setting must be chosen on separate dev images (here ILVR, strength 0.8, N = 16), even when a different, pre-declared comparison (SDEdit) turns out to score better on the test photos.
